quests.instruction: A school badge has exactly four lines of symmetry and looks the same after every quarter turn. Which shape could the badge be?
quests.hint: Test each shape: count its lines of symmetry and check what a quarter turn does.
quests.explanation: A square has 4 lines of symmetry and matches itself after every quarter turn. A rectangle has only 2 lines and matches only after a half turn, and a triangle with three equal sides has 3 lines.
quests.funFact: Many school badges use symmetrical shapes because they look balanced.

quests.instruction: A teacher cuts a square sheet of paper into 4 equal smaller squares to make posters. How does the side of each small poster compare with the side of the big sheet?
options: It is a quarter as long
quests.hint: Picture one cut across the middle and one cut down the middle.
quests.explanation: Two cuts through the middle make 4 equal squares, and each cut halves a length. Each small square has sides half as long as the big square, even though its area is a quarter.
quests.funFact: Halving the side of a square makes its area four times smaller.

quests.instruction: A shelf in a classroom holds a globe, a dictionary, and a pencil tin. Which one is shaped like a cylinder?
quests.hint: Look for the object with two flat round ends joined by a curved side.
quests.explanation: The pencil tin has flat round ends and a curved side, so it is a cylinder. The globe is a sphere and the dictionary is a cuboid.
quests.funFact: A globe is nearly a sphere, though Earth is slightly flattened at the poles.

quests.instruction: A bathroom floor is covered with regular hexagon tiles that fit together with no gaps. At each point where tile corners meet, how many tiles meet?
quests.hint: Each corner of a regular hexagon opens wider than a square corner. How many of them fill all the way around a point?
quests.explanation: Each corner of a regular hexagon measures 120 degrees, and three of them make 360 degrees, a full turn around the point. So 3 tiles meet at each point.
quests.funFact: Bees build honeycomb cells in this same pattern, with three cells meeting at every corner.

quests.instruction: A cereal box is a cuboid 20 cm tall, 15 cm wide, and 5 cm deep. Which faces of the box are the largest?
quests.hint: Work out the area of each pair of faces by multiplying its two measurements.
quests.explanation: The front and back are 20 by 15, which is 300 square cm each. The sides are 20 by 5, which is 100, and the top and bottom are 15 by 5, which is 75.
quests.funFact: Cereal boxes put their biggest faces at the front and back so there is room for pictures and words.

quests.instruction: A lampshade is a cone with its tip cut off, open at the top and the bottom. What flat shapes are its two openings?
quests.hint: Think about the slice you get when you cut a cone straight across.
quests.explanation: Cutting a cone straight across gives a circle, so both openings are circles. The one at the wide end is bigger than the one at the narrow end.
quests.funFact: Many lampshades use this shape because it spreads light downward.

quests.instruction: A toy set has a cube, a cuboid, and a sphere. Which block would be hardest to build a stable tower on?
quests.hint: A tower needs a flat face to rest on.
quests.explanation: A sphere has no flat faces, so it rolls and cannot hold another block steady. A cube and a cuboid have flat faces that stack well.
quests.funFact: Toy building blocks are usually cubes and cuboids for this reason.

quests.instruction: A toy shape sorter has a round hole, a square hole, and a triangle hole. A child pushes a cylinder block into a hole with one of its flat ends first. Which hole does it fit?
quests.hint: Look at the shape of the flat end of the cylinder.
quests.explanation: The flat ends of a cylinder are circles, so the block fits the round hole. A square or triangle hole is the wrong shape.
quests.funFact: A shape sorter shows that each solid has flat faces of particular shapes.

quests.instruction: A toy kit has 12 identical square tiles. Mia arranges them into a rectangle with no gaps or leftover tiles. Which rectangle can she not make?
quests.hint: Multiply the two numbers in each choice and compare the answer with 12.
quests.explanation: 5 by 2 needs 5 × 2 = 10 tiles, not 12. The other rectangles use exactly 12 tiles.
quests.funFact: Twelve tiles can make rectangles in three ways: 1 by 12, 2 by 6, and 3 by 4.

quests.instruction: Engineers add a diagonal bar across a rectangular gate frame. Why does this help?
quests.correctAnswer: It makes two triangles, which cannot be squashed sideways
options: It makes two triangles, which cannot be squashed sideways
It makes the gate a square
quests.hint: Think about which shape stays firm when its corners can pivot.
quests.explanation: A rectangular frame can lean sideways, but a triangle cannot change shape without bending a side. The diagonal splits the rectangle into two triangles, which holds the gate firm.
quests.funFact: Gates and shelves often have a diagonal brace for this reason.

quests.instruction: A playground roundabout has 8 seats spaced equally around the edge. The roundabout turns so that a child moves two seats along. What fraction of a full turn is that?
quests.hint: Eight equal gaps make a full turn. How many gaps does the child move?
quests.explanation: Each gap between seats is one eighth of a turn, and two gaps make 2 out of 8, which is one quarter of a turn.
quests.funFact: Eight seats give eight equal gaps, so each seat-to-seat turn is 45 degrees.

quests.instruction: The side of a playground slide is a right triangle. The ladder side is 3 m tall, and the ground side is 4 m long. How long is the sloping slide?
quests.hint: Think of the 3, 4, 5 triangle.
quests.explanation: A right triangle with short sides of 3 m and 4 m has a longest side of 5 m, which is the sloping slide. Adding 3 + 4 would give 7 m, but the slide is a straight shortcut.
quests.funFact: A straight slope is always shorter than walking along the two shorter sides.

quests.instruction: A small house is a cuboid with a square pyramid for a roof, and the roof's base is the same size as the top of the house. Not counting the floor, how many flat faces can you see from outside?
quests.hint: Count the four walls, then the sloping roof faces.
quests.explanation: The four walls are 4 faces, and the roof has 4 triangular faces, which makes 8. The top of the cuboid is hidden under the roof.
quests.funFact: A roof with four sloping sides is called a hipped roof.

quests.instruction: A window is a rectangle with a half circle on top. How many lines of symmetry does its outline have?
quests.hint: Try folding the window down the middle and across the middle.
quests.explanation: Folding down the middle makes the two halves match, but folding across the middle does not, because the top is curved and the bottom is flat. So there is only 1 line of symmetry.
quests.funFact: Many church windows have this shape.

quests.instruction: A greenhouse is shaped like half of a sphere. What flat shape is its floor?
quests.hint: A flat cut through a sphere gives the same kind of shape each time.
quests.explanation: Cutting a sphere in half leaves a flat circular face, so the floor of the half-sphere greenhouse is a circle.
quests.funFact: Domes shaped like half spheres can cover large spaces without any pillars inside.

quests.instruction: A road sign is a regular octagon. It can be turned by one eighth of a full turn and look exactly the same. How many such turns bring it all the way around?
quests.hint: Eight equal turns make a full turn.
quests.explanation: Each turn is one eighth of a full turn, so 8 of them make a full turn.
quests.funFact: Every regular polygon matches itself after a turn of one full turn divided by its number of sides.

quests.instruction: A traffic cone stands on a square base. Looking straight down from above, which shapes do you see?
quests.hint: The cone part is round, and the base is square.
quests.explanation: From above the round cone looks like a circle, and the square base shows around it as a square.
quests.funFact: Square bases keep traffic cones from rolling away when they are knocked over.

quests.instruction: A rectangular road sign is 90 cm wide and 60 cm tall. A model of the sign is made 3 times smaller in every length. What are the model's measurements?
quests.hint: Divide both measurements by 3.
quests.explanation: 90 ÷ 3 = 30 and 60 ÷ 3 = 20, so the model is 30 cm by 20 cm. It has the same shape as the sign, only smaller.
quests.funFact: Maps and model trains are made by shrinking every length by the same amount.

quests.instruction: Six cans shaped like cylinders are packed in a box in 2 rows of 3. Looking down at the lid of the box, which shape is it?
quests.correctAnswer: A rectangle 3 cans long and 2 cans wide
options: A rectangle 3 cans long and 2 cans wide
quests.hint: The box has to hold two rows of three cans side by side.
quests.explanation: The cans sit in 2 rows of 3, so the box is 3 cans long and 2 cans wide, which is a rectangle.
quests.funFact: A box that holds cans snugly still leaves small gaps, because circles cannot fill a rectangle completely.

quests.instruction: A tube of chips is a cylinder 10 cm tall, and the distance around its circular lid is 20 cm. The label wraps around once with no overlap. What shape and size is the label before it is wrapped?
quests.correctAnswer: A rectangle 20 cm long and 10 cm tall
options: A rectangle 10 cm long and 10 cm tall
A rectangle 20 cm long and 10 cm tall
quests.hint: Unroll the curved side of the cylinder flat.
quests.explanation: The curved side unrolls into a rectangle. It is as tall as the tube, 10 cm, and as long as the distance around the lid, 20 cm.
quests.funFact: Labels on cans and bottles are printed flat and then wrapped around.

quests.instruction: A gift box is a cube with edges 10 cm long. A ribbon goes once around the middle of the box, across four of its faces. How long is the ribbon?
quests.hint: The ribbon crosses four faces, and each crossing is one edge length.
quests.explanation: The ribbon crosses 4 faces and runs 10 cm across each one, so it is 4 × 10 = 40 cm long.
quests.funFact: Ribbon is often tied around the middle of a gift box in exactly this way.

quests.instruction: A pizza box is a square 40 cm on each side. The round pizza inside just touches all four sides of the box. How wide is the pizza?
quests.hint: The pizza touches opposite sides of the box.
quests.explanation: The pizza touches two opposite sides, so its width equals the width of the box, 40 cm.
quests.funFact: Pizza boxes are square because that shape holds a round pizza, stacks well, and folds from one flat sheet.

quests.instruction: A cube-shaped cake is cut into 8 equal small cubes by cutting once through the middle in each direction. How many of the small cubes contain a corner of the original cake?
quests.hint: Think about where each small cube sits in the big cube.
quests.explanation: Each small cube sits in one corner of the big cube, so every one of the 8 small cubes contains one corner of the original.
quests.funFact: A cube has 8 corners, so each small cube gets exactly one.

quests.instruction: A chocolate bar is made of 6 by 4 small squares, 24 squares in all. How many straight breaks are needed to separate it into 24 single squares, if each break splits one piece into two?
quests.hint: Each break makes exactly one more piece.
quests.explanation: You start with 1 piece and each break adds 1 piece, so reaching 24 pieces takes 23 breaks.
quests.funFact: The number of breaks is always one less than the number of pieces, however you break the bar.

quests.instruction: A square photo is shown on a wide rectangular tablet screen, with white bars on both sides of the photo. What does this tell you?
quests.correctAnswer: The screen is wider than it is tall
options: The screen is wider than it is tall
quests.hint: The photo fits the height of the screen, but the screen is longer than that.
quests.explanation: A square photo fits the height of the screen, and since there is room left on both sides, the screen must be wider than it is tall.
quests.funFact: Screens come in different widths, so pictures are sometimes shown with bars to avoid stretching them.

quests.instruction: An artist paints a border by repeating a triangle, a circle, and a square, in that order, starting with the triangle. Which shape is the 31st in the border?
quests.hint: Divide 31 by 3 and look at the remainder.
quests.explanation: 30 shapes make 10 full units, so the 31st shape starts a new unit, which begins with a triangle.
quests.funFact: Every multiple of 3 lands on the square, because the square is the last shape in each unit.

quests.instruction: A game board is an 8 by 8 grid of squares. How many squares are on the outside border, touching the edge of the board?
quests.hint: Count the top row and bottom row, then the squares between them on the left and right.
quests.explanation: The top and bottom rows have 8 squares each, which is 16, and the left and right sides each have 6 more, which is 12, making 28.
quests.funFact: The 36 squares inside the border form a 6 by 6 square.

quests.instruction: A wall panel is 100 cm long and 40 cm tall. Each brick shows a face 20 cm long and 10 cm tall. How many bricks cover the panel with no gaps?
quests.hint: Find how many bricks fit along the length and how many fit up the height.
quests.explanation: Five bricks fit along 100 cm and four fit up 40 cm, so 5 × 4 = 20 bricks.
quests.funFact: Bricklayers offset each row so that the joints do not line up, which makes the wall stronger.

quests.instruction: On a standard dice, opposite faces add up to 7. From one corner you can see the faces 1, 2, and 3. Which numbers are hidden from that view?
quests.hint: Each hidden face is opposite a visible face.
quests.explanation: The hidden faces are opposite the visible ones: opposite 1 is 6, opposite 2 is 5, and opposite 3 is 4.
quests.funFact: You can never see both faces of an opposite pair at the same time.

quests.instruction: A designer wants a stackable block that looks like the same shape from above, from the front, and from the side. Which block should she choose?
options: A cuboid that is long and thin
quests.hint: Check the three views for each solid.
quests.explanation: A cube is a square from above, from the front, and from the side. A cylinder is a circle from above but a rectangle from the sides, and a long thin cuboid shows different rectangles.
quests.funFact: A sphere also looks the same from every direction, but it cannot be stacked.
